sections.title: Basic Concept of Venn Diagrams
sections.content: Venn Diagrams are used to represent relationships between groups (sets). Step 1: Identify all the given sets (A, B, C, etc.). Step 2: Determine which sets are related and which are separate. Step 3: Visualize the relationships as circles. Example: If 'All cats are animals', the circle of Cats will be inside the circle of Animals.

sections.title: Logical Venn Relationships
sections.content: In many questions, relationships are given only in words. Step 1: Check whether one group is completely inside another. Step 2: Check whether two groups partially overlap. Step 3: Check whether groups are completely separate. Example: 'A is completely inside B, and C is separate' means the circle of A is inside B, while C is separate from both.

sections.title: Percentage-Based 2-Set Problems
sections.content: Many questions are given in percentages. Step 1: Identify both percentages. Step 2: If total population is given, convert percentages into numbers. Step 3: Estimate or calculate the overlap. Example: If 60% people read A and 50% read B, then at least 10% people may read both.

sections.title: Venn Diagram Fill Method
sections.content: Step 1: Fill the intersection (common part) first. Step 2: Then fill the remaining parts of each set separately. Step 3: Finally verify the total. This method reduces calculation mistakes.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Counting the overlap twice. 2. Placing circles inside the wrong set. 3. Making mistakes while converting percentages into numbers. 4. Confusing union and intersection.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Venn Diagrams, relationships between sets are represented using circles. Identify logical relationships, apply mathematical formulas, and convert percentages correctly in percentage-based questions.

tricks.title: Inside Rule
tricks.explanation: If it is stated that 'All A are B', the circle of A will be inside the circle of B.

tricks.title: Separate Rule
tricks.explanation: If two groups are completely different, their circles will not overlap.
tricks.example: Cats and Cars have no relation.

tricks.title: Overlap Identification
tricks.explanation: If 'Some A are B', the circles will partially overlap.

tricks.title: Fill the Common Part First
tricks.explanation: Filling the intersection first makes calculations easier.
tricks.example: Place the people who read both newspapers first.

tricks.title: Percentage Conversion
tricks.explanation: If the total population is assumed to be 100, percentages directly convert into numbers.

tricks.title: Avoid Double Counting
tricks.explanation: Do not count the overlapping group twice.

tricks.title: Total Check Method
tricks.explanation: At the end, add all parts and match them with the total.
tricks.example: If the total is 100 people, the sum should also be 100.
